newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: RAM assigns A2 to AMMB unsecured bonds.
newsitem.headline: RAM assigns A2 to AMMB unsecured bonds.

text.p: Rating Agency Malaysia Bhd (RAM) said on Thursday it had assigned a long-term rating of A2 to AMMB Holdings Bhd's 445.25 million ringgit redeemable unsecured bonds with warrants.
In a statement, RAM said the rating reflects the credit strength of AMMB Holdings' subsidiaries which are expected to be the main contributors of dividend payments.
The key subsidiaries mentioned are Arab-Malaysian Merchant Bank Bhd, Arab-Malaysian Finance Bhd and Arab-Malaysian Securities Holding Sdn Bhd.
RAM had accorded a long-term rating of A1 to the merchant bank and a short-term rating of P1 to the finance company.
The four-year 115 million ringgit revolving underwritten notes issuance facility of Arab-Malaysian Securities Holding's main unit, Arab-Malaysian Securities, was given a short-term rating of P2.
The rating for AMMB Holdings also took into consideration the expected inadequate accumulation of dividend income to repay the bond obligations, RAM said.
It also considered the expected reliance on proceeds from the exercise of warrants to meet the redemption of the bonds upon maturity.
